visual.glance_promise: Do not learn all of supply chain. Learn the next decision your work affects.
visual.primary_reading_route: home function -> one directional transfer gate -> adjacent decision language -> ownership boundary -> next-meeting question

core_units.visual_teaches: Use the demand signal as adjacent language before treating price or lead time as the only supplier-conversation input.
Translate the plan into the capacity question the next specialist must resolve.
Connect a production constraint to the delivery promise another team must manage.
Frame movement and freight choices through the commitment they protect or put at risk.
Ask which operator decision an analysis should make easier before building another report.
Test whether a strategic idea can be described as a changed frontline workflow or decision.

caption.job: Explain why generic cross-functional advice stalls, state the ownership boundary, and invite the reader to identify the adjacent decision they need to understand. It should not narrate all six routes again.
adds: The reason broad cross-functional advice is difficult to turn into an action.
The ownership boundary: adjacent literacy does not replace specialist depth.
The next-meeting question that turns the framework into a conversation.
must_not_repeat: All six function-to-decision translations in caption bullets when the visual already provides the complete reference.

hook.job: Name the gap between 'be more cross-functional' and choosing what to learn next, without revealing the six-route answer in the opening.
hook.why_this_mode: The visual owns the reusable reference. A direct hook would also be valid if it made the reader promise clearer; curiosity is not treated as a universal reach rule.

review.notes: The linked caption currently repeats all six route concepts in bullets. Keep the framing, boundary, and next-meeting question, but remove the route-by-route restatement before this draft can pass choreography review.
